slot.brief: A car (or body) on a level/curved track negotiating a turn at a given speed; find the minimum coefficient of static friction required, or analyse banking with friction — resolving forces along radial and vertical directions.

stem: A car moves at $10\sqrt{2}$ m s$^{-1}$ on a banked circular track of radius $20$ m. The banking angle is $30^\circ$. Find the minimum coefficient of static friction needed to prevent slipping. Take $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.

verdicts.working: Here, v²/(rg)=1. Since this exceeds tan 30°, friction acts down the bank. Resolving forces gives μ=(cos 30°−sin 30°)/(cos 30°+sin 30°)=2−√3.

working:
$a_c=v^2/r=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}>g\tan30^\circ$; friction acts down the bank.
$N\sin30^\circ+f\cos30^\circ=ma_c$.
$N\cos30^\circ-f\sin30^\circ=mg$.
$\mu_s=\dfrac{f}{N}=\dfrac{a_c\cos30^\circ-g\sin30^\circ}{g\cos30^\circ+a_c\sin30^\circ}=2-\sqrt{3}$
